source.title: Streaming Convolutional Neural Networks for End-to-End Learning With Multi-Megapixel Images
source.authors: H. Pinckaers; B. van Ginneken; Geert Litjens

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training loss and accuracy for a CNN trained from a shared initialization with conventional training and streaming. It does not measure training error on the benchmarks or conditions named by most versions.
record.gate_note: The ImageNette experiment reports training curves for conventional and streaming training. TUPAC16 and CAMELYON17 report task performance, not training classification error. The text cites prior work on initialization and batch normalization but does not test those comparisons here.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates a memory-saving training implementation and downstream task performance. Its ImageNette experiment tests equivalence between streaming and conventional training, without testing sufficiently large networks reaching near-zero training error or any other claim version. Initialization and batch normalization are recipe choices, without controlled comparisons of their optimization effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for ImageNette: streaming closely matches conventional training, with small later numerical differences that do not appear to harm performance. The broader conclusion is that streaming enables end-to-end training on multi-megapixel images and that increased resolution generally improves the evaluated pathology tasks.
record.recipe_differences: Tests a streaming implementation against conventional training on ImageNette; it does not reproduce the CIFAR training-error recipes in the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Training method (conventional versus streaming) produces nearly identical loss curves, with small later differences.

fits_no_version.finding: From the same initialization, streaming and conventional ImageNette training have nearly identical loss curves, with small later differences attributed to floating-point arithmetic.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Tiled streaming with reconstructed gradients preserves conventional CNN training behavior while reducing memory requirements.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
record.problems: Figure 2 is the only reported ImageNette training-accuracy result; the text does not state its numerical values or a training-error metric. The ImageNette subset contains 100 examples per class and is not one of the benchmarks named in V1.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error for sufficiently large CIFAR networks, including corrupted labels, and its dependence on capacity, stopping or regularization.
Teacher-student local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Effects of initialization on training speed and trainable depth; no initialization comparison is reported.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery, curvature dynamics and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and equivalence with Fixup; no corresponding comparison is reported.

record.verdict_notes: The CAMELYON17 recipe replaces batch normalization with weight decay and LSUV initialization to address exploding gradients, but reports no controlled before-and-after optimization result. This does not establish a verdict on V4 or V6.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, model-size scaling, Adam, or whether a sufficiently large network reaches near-zero training error. ImageNette results are shown only in Figure 2.

rows.subject: CNN (normal)
rows.size_stated: Architecture in Table II: convolutional channels 16, 32, 64, 128, 256; 10 output classes.

conditions.value: ImageNette subset; 100 examples of each of 10 classes

rows.note: Figure 2 shows the training accuracy curve and plotted values, but the text gives no numerical training-accuracy result. The curve remains substantially below perfect accuracy.
rows.check: This is a baseline for the study's implementation comparison, not a test of V1. Subperfect accuracy on an augmented ImageNette training stream does not establish a limitation on sufficiently large networks fitting CIFAR training labels. Section V-A specifies 100 training images per class and a separate 100 tuning images per class; training lasted 300 epochs although Figure 2 displays 200.

rows.subject: CNN (streaming)
rows.size_stated: Architecture in Table II: convolutional channels 16, 32, 64, 128, 256; 10 output classes.
rows.operation_detail: Streaming training, dividing the input into four tiles.

conditions.value: ImageNette subset; 100 examples of each of 10 classes

rows.note: Compared with conventional training; Figure 2 shows the training accuracy curve and plotted values, but the text gives no numerical training-accuracy result. The curve remains substantially below perfect accuracy.
rows.check: This measures the study's streaming implementation against conventional training and should not be a claim-evidence row. Neither network capacity sufficient for interpolation nor error on the fixed training examples is established. Training lasted 300 epochs although Figure 2 displays 200.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
